 svg]:hover:fill-accent-color"> svg]:inline"> Pooh Shiesty is allegedly kept in his jail cell for 23 hours a day, and his codefendant Big30 let him know he and their fans are behind him. div>p>iframe]:w-full [&>div>p>iframe]:aspect-video

One of these codefendants, Big30, took to his Instagram recently to share a message of support for Shiesty amid his reported struggles and restrictions behind bars, as caught by No Jumper on Twitter.
 "As we fight this case together we still got all the club venues and arenas going crazy," he wrote. "I'm on house arrest you in a cell they going crazy like we present... NEVER GIVE UP ON US WE GOD FAVORITE."
 Big30 performed Pooh Shiesty's "FDO" for high school students a month and a half ago, so he has been able to witness fans' support firsthand. For those unaware, the Memphis rapper is currently on house arrest with various restrictions, although he has still been able to engage in activities like that event.
 As for the other Memphis MC's issues, Pooh's legal team claims authorities are unlawfully keeping him in his jail cell for 23 hours a day. He's also allegedly not getting his minimum visitation hours per month, which is affecting his mental health.
 Read More: Eminem’s Kid Rock Collaboration Is A Betrayal Of Who He Used To Be 
 When Is Pooh Shiesty's Trial?
 For those unaware, Pooh Shiesty and Big30's Gucci Mane case also involves Shiesty's father and six other codefendants. Federal authorities accused them of holding Guwop in a Dallas studio, extorting him, and robbing him of personal items in order to sign Shiesty out of his contract with 1017 Records.
 If everything goes according to the current schedule, the trial on these robbery and kidnapping charges will begin in February of 2027. The defendants pleaded not guilty to the charges against them, and there's been a lot of drama in the hip-hop world over this case, snitching allegations and more.
 While Big30 is free, Pooh Shiesty was denied bond. This also continues to cause controversy, especially with the aforementioned allegations from Pooh's legal team.
 We will see what other developments emerge ahead of trial and how these issues of incarceration and pre-trial freedom continue to develop. Big30 and fans of these artists continue to show their support, whether it's online or by enjoying their music in public settings.

About The Author
 Gabriel Bras Nevares 
 (30 Articles published)
 --> Gabriel Bras Nevares is a staff writer for HotNewHipHop. He joined HNHH while completing his B.A. in Journalism & Mass Communication at The George Washington University in the summer of 2022. 
Born and raised in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Gabriel treasures the crossover between his native reggaetón and hip-hop news coverage, such as his review for Bad Bunny’s hometown concert in 2024. But more specifically, he digs for the deeper side of hip-hop conversations, whether that’s the “death” of the genre in 2023, the lyrical and parasocial intricacies of the Kendrick Lamar and Drake battle, or the many moving parts of the Young Thug and YSL RICO case. 
Beyond engaging and breaking news coverage, Gabriel makes the most out of his concert obsessions, reviewing and recapping festivals like Rolling Loud Miami and Camp Flog Gnaw. He’s also developed a strong editorial voice through album reviews, think-pieces, and interviews with some of the genre’s brightest upstarts and most enduring obscured gems like Homeboy Sandman, Bktherula, Bas, and Devin Malik.
